reason: Measurements verified exactly by driving the master at 1440x960: publish ink runs 115.4-442.8 with the page box ending at 539 and 517px of identical ground below it; owner-empty's .b-empty ends at 677; the day device sits 92.8-659.5, i.e. 94 above and 300 below. The cause is a real plumbing failure rather than taste: shell.css line 139 declares `.tl-page { min-height: 100% }`, but its parent `#tl` carries only `min-height: 100%` and no definite height, so the percentage resolves to auto and the page box collapses to content height (539 / 700 / 773 against a 960 viewport). The composition the shell intended - a page that occupies the frame - is written and silently does not take effect, and nothing in the gates or in lessons.md covers it. So the observation is confirmed. The FIX AS WRITTEN is refuted: applied verbatim it makes all three states worse. It adds min-height to a block nested inside padded ancestors, so at 1440x960 every state that previously fitted now scrolls (publish 960->981, owner-empty 960->1057, day 960->1051), and at 768x1024 all three scroll too; it inflates the day phone mock from 567px to 918px, taller than any phone; it does nothing at all to owner-empty at 390x844 (that block already overflows at 767px); and the 190px constant is invented - the real chrome is 40px stage padding plus 48/56 field padding plus, on owner-empty, the bar. It also aims at b.css when the anchoring lives in shell.css and would leave directions A and C top-anchored on the same states. One factual correction to the finding: the 301px below the day card is lab-stage ground beneath a 390px device mock, not the artifact's own frame; the real-phone equivalent is day ending at 565 in an 844 viewport, which is the number worth fixing.
sharpenedFix: Fix it in shell.css, where the anchoring lives, and make the declared intent actually resolve. (1) `.tl-page { min-height: 100dvh; }` - replaces the dead `min-height: 100%`, and dvh is right for the phone toolbar. (2) Centre only the states that are one object on a bare ground, using SAFE centring so nothing can ever be clipped or pushed out of reach: `[data-state="publish"] .tl-page, [data-state="day"] .tl-page, [data-state="ended"] .tl-page, [data-state="loading"] .tl-page { justify-content: safe center; }`. Verified: no new scrollHeight at 1440x960, 1280x900, 768x1024, 390x844 or 390x520; owner-flight and print are untouched at every width; day lands 140..704 in an 844 phone instead of 0..565, publish 251..709 at 1440, ended 230..730, loading 301..659. `safe` degrades to flex-start the moment content exceeds the viewport (confirmed at 390x520). (3) owner-empty must NOT be centred this way - it carries the .b-bar, which is chrome and belongs on the top edge. Centre its body between the bar and the bottom instead: `[data-state="owner-empty"] .tl-stage { display: flex; flex-direction: column; flex: 1 1 auto; } [data-state="owner-empty"] .b-field { flex: 1 1 auto; display: flex; flex-direction: column; } [data-state="owner-empty"] .b-empty { flex: 1 1 auto; display: grid; align-content: center; }`. Verified: the bar stays at 115..167 at 1440 and 768 while the title moves 349->442, no new scroll, and 390 (where the block already overflows) is unchanged. Drop the `padding-bottom: 7vh` optical bias entirely, or express it as `padding-bottom: min(6vh, 56px)` inside the centred rule only - as written it is a viewport-scaled constant that re-creates the overflow the fix exists to remove. Re-run audit.mjs and interaction-check.mjs after, since this changes the composited geometry the contrast and hit-target checks measure.
